studyRole: Post-study design experiment for the portfolio, run as one shuffled batch per provider. Not part of the HAI 2026 paper.
background: In the vote-facts batch (2026-10-05), stating three fit facts on the shelf removed most order-caused errors (41 -> 2 DeepSeek, 66 -> 7 MiMo); swaps that remained were almost all between equally good products. Re-asking in a random order before writing to the record kept most wrong picks out but also held about half the right ones, and after the results most of those were found to be ties the order had broken. The two parts were never tested together, and the 'ties should be held' reading was made after the results. This experiment tests the two together, with that reading written down before running.
question: With facts on the shelf (F1) and one random-order re-ask before the record (P1), how many wrong picks and how many order-decided picks reach the person's record, compared with today's platform (no facts, everything written), and how many order-stable right picks does the door wrongly hold?

units.source: artifacts/vote-facts/units.json (920 product-language shelves with facts and the platform's random orders), sha256 ff5e848799914d856b08fb213f7155ee01f5e5678199d120a830e9fdd473b98a. Unchanged.

providers.deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash, /chat/completions, thinking disabled, temperature 0, JSON mode, max 96 output tokens; V9 system instruction verbatim
providers.mimo: mimo-v2.5, /responses, reasoning effort none, temperature 0, json_object, max 96 output tokens; V9 instruction verbatim

design: 2 x 2 within one batch: shelf (L0 plain / F1 facts, payloads exactly as in vote-facts) x door (P0 write everything / P1 write only if a random-order re-ask picks the same product). All calls are new (cache scope 'shelf-door/...'); nothing is reused from earlier batches, because identical requests drifted between batches (4.5% DeepSeek, 28.4% MiMo).

conditions.label: Each product carries isRequestedType, hasRequestedAttribute, withinBudget; no instruction added

slots.immediate-a: the served order: the pick the platform would write
slots.held-a, held-b: the other study arm's order, twice: the probe for whether order decided the pick
slots.sham-a: the served order a third time: the door's noise (a re-ask that is not a new order)
slots.random1-a: the platform's own random order: the door's re-ask (P1)

classification.selection: immediate-a is a product. Abandons and protocol failures write nothing under any policy.
classification.wrong: a selection that does not meet every constraint (frozen V9 evaluation).
classification.orderDecided: a selection where held-a == held-b and both differ from immediate-a: the other order consistently leads elsewhere. Includes ties the order broke and errors the order caused. One probe order only, so this undercounts.
classification.stableRight: a selection that meets every constraint and where held-a == held-b == immediate-a.
classification.unclear: held-a != held-b; reported, not used in the rule.

policies.P0-writeAll: every selection is written to the record
policies.P1-oneReask: write the selection iff random1-a is the same product
policies.P2-twoReasks: write iff random1-a and random2-a are both the same product (F1 only, secondary)

primary.wrongWritten: W = wrong selections written. Compared: today's platform T = (L0, P0) against the combined design D = (F1, P1).
primary.orderDecidedWritten: O = order-decided selections written, T against D.
primary.stableRightHeld: H = stable-right selections under F1 that P1 holds / stable-right selections under F1. Holding an order-decided pick is the intended behaviour and is not counted here.

secondary: the four cells (L0,P0), (L0,P1), (F1,P0), (F1,P1): W, O, right selections written, stable-right selections written
door noise: P1 with sham-a in place of random1-a under F1, same counts
shelf replication: S and U (as in check-first, without noise floors), L0 vs F1
success rate over the four main slots (V9 rule)

analysis.uncertainty: Cluster bootstrap over tasks, resampled within category, both recommender families kept together. 4000 replicates, seed 20261006. Percentile 95% intervals for counts, differences and H.
analysis.reductionShare: share removed = 1 - D / T, for W and for O.
analysis.pooling: None. Each provider is read on its own.

decisionRule.works: W: share removed >= 0.8 and the 95% interval of D - T lies entirely below 0; O: share removed >= 0.5 and its interval lies entirely below 0; H: point estimate <= 0.2.

readingsWrittenBeforeRunning.works: Shelf and door together: the record receives almost no wrong picks and far fewer picks the order decided, while order-stable right picks still get through. The design can be shown as tested end to end, for these two models and this storefront.
readingsWrittenBeforeRunning.costly: The combination keeps wrong and order-decided picks out, but also holds too many picks the order did not decide; the door needs a better re-ask (more orders, or the agent's own tie report) before it is usable.
readingsWrittenBeforeRunning.partial: The shelf keeps wrong picks out, but one random re-ask does not catch the ties; the door as designed does not do its job.
readingsWrittenBeforeRunning.doesNotWork: Reported as found; the vote-facts result does not replicate in this batch.
readingsWrittenBeforeRunning.always: Facts are exact by construction (computed from the tokens and price that define success), so W under F1 is an upper bound on what real catalogue data would achieve.

execution.callOrder: All calls for a provider (920 x 12 = 11,040) shuffled together.
execution.smokeTest: First 5 units (sorted), both conditions; kept in the dataset.
execution.invalidOutputPolicy: As before: up to two retries with the retry note; a third failure is __PROTOCOL_FAILURE__.
execution.stopOnPayment: On HTTP 402 the run cancels the remaining calls and exits; it resumes from cache after a top-up.

claimBoundary: Categorical outputs of two model versions over cleaned Amazon product titles, brands and prices in a research storefront. Fit facts are derived from frozen title tokens and prices; success and regret are benchmark measures, not human utility; 'order-decided' uses one alternative order. Says nothing about human users, other models, other wordings, or production retailers.
